title: Ops→Sales Incident Walkthrough — Pocket Guide (Draft)
content:
Purpose: Short, portable deck and one-pager for sellers to use during or immediately after an operational incident. Goal is: help Sales keep deals calm, set correct expectations, capture buy signals, and route technical follow-ups to the right partner (SRE, solutions engineering, customer success) without overpromising.

Audience: AEs, SEs, ACs, SDRs who get pinged by current or prospective customers about a platform incident, outage, or degraded performance. Also helpful as a rapid enablement for new sellers.

How to use:
- Keep this open on your laptop/phone during incident communications.
- Use the TL;DR script first (first 30–90s). If technical questions follow, hand to assigned technical responder.
- Log call notes into CRM and tag with jira key if provided by SRE.

Deck / Pocket Guide outline (compact, 6 slides plus appendix):
1) TL;DR for sellers (1 slide)
  - Key statement (script): "We’re aware of an incident affecting [feature/region]. Our SRE team has an active incident response and is working on a remediation plan. We'll share an ETA for full recovery within the next X minutes and provide updates at Y cadence. I'm staying on this and will connect you to technical support if you want deeper details."
  - When to escalate to SEs/SREs: customer asks for architecture-level root cause, custom deployment questions, or legal/compliance implications.

2) Quick customer-facing FAQ (1 slide)
  - "Is my data safe?" -> "Yes, no evidence of data exfiltration; we are preserving audit logs and will share findings once validated."
  - "When will it be fixed?" -> "SRE will give an ETA; expect proactive updates every 15–30 minutes depending on severity."
  - "Will I be refunded or compensated?" -> "Compensation/credits are handled case-by-case; we will route this through your CSM and our revenue ops team."

3) Severity taxonomy & expected seller wording (1 slide)
  - Severity P0 (outage): immediate wording, commit to hourly updates, offer warm handoff to SRE.
  - Severity P1 (degraded but functional): acknowledge impact, offer workaround if known, schedule follow-up.
  - Severity P2/P3 (minor or localized): reassure and monitor, no immediate escalation unless customer requests.

4) What SRE will and will not provide to Sales (1 slide)
  - Will provide: status, ETA ranges, remediation steps, relevant JIRA/incident ID, whether customer-specific mitigations are required.
  - Will not provide immediately: definitive root cause, postmortem analysis, or deployment-level secrets. Use measured language.

5) Short scripts: Hand-off, Close, Follow-up (1 slide)
  - Hand-off to SRE/SE script: "I'd like to bring in our SRE/SE to walk through the technical details — can we schedule a short join? They will share the incident id and next steps."
  - Closing script after an update: "Thanks for your patience. We’ll share the next update by [time]. Can I confirm your contact preferences for follow-ups?"
  - Reassurance for prospects: "This is an operational incident; our platform has multiple built-in fallbacks and redundant paths — we’ll share the timeline and mitigation plan shortly."

6) After-action checklist for Sales (1 slide)
  - Create CRM note + incident ID tag.
  - Capture customer impact (scope, duration, feature area).
  - Book a post-incident technical review with SE/SRE if customer requests.
  - Flag large ARR or legal-risk accounts to revenue ops and legal.

Appendix (quick references)
- Contacts: On-call SRE (rotations), dedicated SEs, CSM handoff email templates.
- Quick link matrix: public status page, internal incident dashboard, claim/credit policy doc.
- Sample email to send after incident resolution.

Sample scripts (copy/paste friendly)
- TL;DR (30s): "Thank you for the heads up — we’ve got an active incident impacting the Redwood inference service in [region/feature]. Our SRE team is actively working on it and will confirm an ETA in the next [15/30] minutes. I’ll keep you updated and connect you with our technical lead if you’d like deeper details now."
- Escalation request (to SRE via Slack/jira): "Customer [name] on call impacted by incident [ID]. Asking for 1:1 runthrough and any available mitigations; please advise ETA and whether a temporary routing change can help."

Real-world scenario examples (2 short vignettes)
- Prospective customer in POC notices degraded token throughput during demo: Use TL;DR, escalate to SE for transparent walkthrough, offer to pause/demo on alternate model or lower token rates, log as high-touch POC.
- Existing enterprise customer sees regional outage affecting embeddings: Use severity P0 script, offer to route traffic to Dedicated instances (if available) as temporary mitigation, ensure legal and CSM looped for credits discussion.

Do's and Don'ts (one-liners)
- Do: Acknowledge quickly, commit to update cadence, loop in CSM for compensation conversations.
- Don’t: Promise root cause or timeline beyond what SRE has given, speculate about data loss, or publicly post internal ticket ids without approval.

Open questions & next iterations (for this draft)
- Add a one-click CRM macro that auto-populates incident tags and SRE contact? (engineering + sales automation work)
- Add a condensed mobile-first one-pager for reps on phones?
- Include a short training video (<3 min) with roleplay examples.

Immediate next steps (owner: Ava)
- Run this draft by Ravi (SRE lead) and Janelle (Head of SE) for technical accuracy by 2024-11-12.
- Create CRM macros and Slack snippet templates in the next sprint.
- Pilot with 5 AEs for two weeks and iterate based on feedback.

Notes to reviewers: This is intentionally seller-centric and non-technical. The goal is to avoid swampy technical detail, reduce seller anxiety, and create a repeatable handoff pattern to protect the customer's trust and reduce churn risk.
